evidence.title: Mission termination after RCS activation
evidence.body: Both rings of the reentry control system have been activated to regain control, and substantial propellant has been used. Under these conditions, mission rules require termination. Cancel the remaining objectives and prepare a contingency return.

provenance.note: Automatic at briefing; reference. Historical termination principle H2; game selection boundary F7.

evidence.title: Network coverage and report timing
evidence.body: The last report tells us what was true when the crew sent it. Between tracking passes, we have no new information about their condition. Keep the report's observation time beside it; mark anything since that time as unconfirmed. The crew must act on their own until the next station acquires their signal.

provenance.note: Automatic at briefing; instructional reference grounded in H1.

evidence.title: Contact drill: instruction and readback
evidence.body: Houston CAPCOM sends the instruction to the tracking-ship CAPCOM, who reads it back and confirms receipt. FLIGHT checks the confirmation before treating the instruction as received. Mark missing observation times as unknown.

provenance.note: Acquired by g8-prep-contact; original F1 reference. Named practice calls and desk roles are original game exercises, not a claim that these exact rehearsals occurred before Gemini VIII.

evidence.title: Recovery drill: pickup instruction
evidence.body: Elias passes the aircraft's location report to the DoD recovery coordinator. They identify the desk that will send the ship its pickup instruction and check the readback. Record aircraft support and the ship's arrival separately.

provenance.note: Acquired by g8-prep-recovery; original F2 reference. Named practice calls and desk roles are original game exercises, not a claim that these exact rehearsals occurred before Gemini VIII.

evidence.title: Systems drill: low-propellant warning
evidence.body: Mara reports the RCS propellant warning to FLIGHT and CAPCOM together. She states what the instruments show, what remains uncertain, and the response she recommends for entry. CAPCOM reads the recommendation back before passing it on.

provenance.note: Acquired by g8-prep-systems; original F3 reference. Named practice calls and desk roles are original game exercises, not a claim that these exact rehearsals occurred before Gemini VIII.

evidence.title: Docking confirmed.
evidence.body: The crew have confirmed docking with Agena.

provenance.note: Docking event; H3. No roll data appended during gap.

evidence.title: Emergency report through the tracking ship.
evidence.body: The crew report an uncontrolled tumble after undocking. The report reaches the ground through Coastal Sentry Quebec.

evidence.title: Crew regain control.
evidence.body: The crew have used the reentry control system to stabilize the spacecraft. The remaining mission objectives must be relinquished.

evidence.title: Return opportunities
evidence.body: Both opportunities return the crew to the western Pacific. An earlier landing gets them off the damaged spacecraft sooner, but the ship is hours away. Another orbit brings them down closer to the recovery force, with less RCS propellant left for entry.

provenance.note: Automatic at return planning; F7 simulated planning report. Western Pacific historical context only is H2.

evidence.title: Aircraft and recovery ship positions
evidence.body: Aircraft can support either return. At the earlier landing point, the nearest ship is hours away. At the later point, the recovery force can reach the capsule sooner.

provenance.note: Automatic at return planning; F4/F7. No real coordinates or ships assigned.

evidence.title: RCS propellant remaining
evidence.body: The spacecraft is stable for now. The reentry control system, or RCS, uses small thrusters to control its attitude during entry. Propellant is limited; using more before entry leaves less for that task. Mara is checking the remaining supply.

provenance.note: Automatic at return planning; F7. This is not actual Gemini VIII telemetry.

evidence.title: Pickup instruction confirmed
evidence.body: Elias and the DoD coordinator have agreed who sends the final pickup instruction to the ship. The readback is complete. This should prevent confusion during the approach, but the ship still has to reach the capsule.

provenance.note: Automatic at planning only if recovery preparation selected; F2/F7.

evidence.title: Warning call checked
evidence.body: Mara has checked the call with FLIGHT and CAPCOM. Both desks know to expect the RCS warning and her recommendation together, so CAPCOM can pass the instruction without waiting for the assessment to be repeated.

provenance.note: Automatic at planning only if systems preparation selected; F3/F7.

evidence.title: Instruction receipt checked
evidence.body: CAPCOM has identified who sends the next instruction and who confirms its receipt. Until that confirmation comes back, FLIGHT will treat the instruction as pending. The same check applies to either return.

provenance.note: Automatic at planning only if contact preparation selected; F1/F7.

evidence.title: Both crew members aboard the recovery ship.
evidence.body: Armstrong and Scott have been recovered alive. Their condition and the course of this return are recorded below.

provenance.note: Only at actual modeled pickup event. Alive recovery has H3 context; branch details F7.

evidence.title: Disagreement after Gemini VIII
evidence.body: Post-flight analysis has cleared Armstrong and Scott of blame. Walt Cunningham has criticized aspects of their performance; Tom Stafford has argued that undocking from Agena was the wrong decision. Gene Kranz has identified a failure on the ground: too few contingency procedures for the docked phase. Frank Borman and Wally Schirra have defended the crew.

provenance.note: Automatic only in the later post-flight scene. Attributed paraphrase of H5, a secondary account; not a transcript or an investigation document reproduced here.
